findings.title: queued timestamp is fixed at import time
findings.body: AssignmentSource.queued uses timezone.now() as a dataclass default, which is evaluated once when the class body runs, not when an instance is created. Every AssignmentSource therefore shares the same queued value from process import, so the field cannot record when an inbound assignment was actually queued. It needs field(default_factory=timezone.now) (or an explicit argument). As written, any later ordering, dedupe, or staleness check on queued is wrong.

findings.title: Celery kwargs include a raw datetime
findings.body: sync_group_assignee_outbound passes assignment_source.to_dict() straight into sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async. asdict() leaves queued as a datetime, which is not JSON-serializable. Sentry task messages are JSON-encoded, and the new tests only run tasks in-process, so they never hit the broker encoder. In production, every inbound assign/deassign that sets an AssignmentSource will raise when the outbound task is enqueued. That aborts sync_group_assignee_inbound after the Sentry assignee write and drops outbound sync to every other linked integration, not only the originating one. to_dict/from_dict need a JSON-safe queued value (for example an ISO string parsed back to datetime); from_dict currently does cls(**input_dict) and also returns None on TypeError, which would fail open and re-enable the sync loop if the payload cannot be rebuilt.
